title: Content-aware prefix merge for embedding cache to reduce duplicate computation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our embeddings endpoint sees a large fraction of requests that share common prefixes (short queries, repeated system prompts, or identical document headers). Current prefix cache keys are strict string prefixes or content hashes, which causes redundant compute when semantically-equivalent prefixes are tokenized differently (whitespace/ punctuation/ Unicode variants) or when partially overlapping input sequences exist. We also see cache blowup from high-cardinality near-duplicates and inconsistent invalidation across replicas.

Proposal: Implement a content-aware prefix merging layer for the embeddings cache that reduces duplicate embedding computation without sacrificing correctness. Key components: 1) Prefix canonicalization pipeline (Unicode NFKC, trim/normalize whitespace, simple punctuation collapse where safe, lowercasing configurable per model), 2) Tokenization-aware shingle fingerprints that produce a canonical fingerprint for semantically identical prefixes even if raw strings differ, 3) Merge rules that allow multiple similar prefixes to map to a single cache entry when cosine similarity of embeddings between freshly-sampled canonical prefixes falls above a tuned threshold, 4) Non-blocking background warm-writes to populate merged keys on a best-effort basis, 5) Generation-based invalidation (small monotonic generation ID per write) to avoid race conditions across replicas, and 6) Hierarchical TTLs and adaptive eviction (short TTL for high-churn keys, longer for stable system prompts).

Why different from previous efforts: Prior tickets focused on fingerprint LRU, dedupe TTLs and compact windows. This ticket is about merging near-duplicate prefixes at the content/tokenization level and adding a correctness-first merge gate (similarity threshold + canary metrics) that reduces end-to-end token compute by avoiding redundant forward passes for semantically equivalent inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Cache hit rate for prefix keys increases by >= 18% on synthetic dataset with 60% prefix overlap compared to baseline
End-to-end embedding latency P95 decreases by >= 10% for mixed prefix workloads under production QPS without increasing P99 by > 3%
No measurable degradation in reranking quality: NDCG@10 delta <= 0.005 on held-out rerank benchmark after merge enabled
Rollout gated behind feature flag and canary traffic; rollback within 15 minutes via flag
Generation-based invalidation prevents stale embeddings from being served across replica restarts (integration tests pass)
implementation_notes: Add canonicalization module in embedding service: normalize_unicode -> collapse_safe_punct -> trim_spaces -> optional lowercase (model-config driven)
Tokenize canonicalized prefix with model tokenizer to create token shingles (n=3 by default) and compute BPE-aware rolling hash fingerprint
Maintain a small similarity cache for short prefixes: precompute embeddings for canonicalized prefixes on write and compare via cosine against existing merged-key centers
Use a conservative merge threshold (start 0.98 cosine) and an instrumentation experiment to lower threshold in increments while monitoring quality metrics

Implement non-blocking background writes: on first request mapped to a merged key, return embedding after computing, and asynchronously write both native key and merged key to cache with generation ID
Extend cache entry schema to include: canonical_form (string), token_fingerprint (string), generation_id (int) and center_embedding (float32 blob) — stored as metadata in backing Redis/rocksdb layer
Eviction: integrate with existing windowed-LRU and memory-aware allocator; give merged keys a slightly higher cost (so they are less likely to be evicted prematurely) and use hierarchical TTLs
Invalidation: support tombstones with generation checks; when a model/version rollout invalidates embeddings, bump generation and propagate tombstone with TTL to avoid immediate re-population storms
Replica consistency: writes are best-effort; readers always check generation_id and fall back to computing fresh embedding if mismatch
API compatibility: no changes to external embeddings API surface; behavior controlled by runtime flag and model config per-customer
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization and token_fingerprint determinism (including hard Unicode corners and punctuation variants)
Integration tests for generation-based invalidation across 3-replica local cluster
Benchmark harness: replay production prefix-heavy traffic with and without merge enabled to measure hit-rate, latency, and token-cost reduction
Quality evaluation: run reranking pipeline on held-out queries to compute cosine drift and NDCG deltas for merged-key policy at different thresholds
Chaos test: simulate replica restart and cache tombstone propagation; ensure no stale embeddings served
A/B rollout: canary 1% traffic for 48h, evaluate embeddings quality and customer-facing metrics before expanding to 10/50/100%
rollout_plan: Feature flagged behind runtime config and per-customer opt-in
Canary phase: 1% traffic, monitor embedding quality metrics, P95/P99 latency, cache hit ratio, and tail error rates
Ramp phases: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over weeks with hold windows at each stage and predefined success gates
Fallback: runtime flag off or per-model disable; immediate stop of merged-key reads and rely on native prefix cache
Post-rollout: schedule 2-week observation window and automated alerts for cache miss spikes or quality regression
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive merging causes quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative default threshold, run A/B quality checks and fail-safe rollback
Risk: Increased memory due to storing center embeddings and metadata. Mitigation: hierarchical TTLs and give merged-keys higher eviction cost to manage churn, track memory pressure metrics
Risk: Race conditions across replicas leading to transient stale reads. Mitigation: generation IDs and read-time generation checks; tombstone propagation
Risk: Tokenizer drift between models breaks fingerprint equivalence. Mitigation: per-model tokenizer fingerprinting and do not merge across incompatible tokenizer configs
Risk: Added complexity in cache store schema impacting upgrade path. Mitigation: backward compatible schema changes with feature flags and migration tool
